title: 35 播客一周年｜我们试着做了法国哲学高考题……
title_en: Podcast Anniversary Special: We Tried Answering a French Philosophy Bac Exam Question
summary_cn: 《抑扬格》一周年特别节目：两位主播即兴作答法国哲学高考题「真理是否总是具有说服力？」——从地球是圆是平、现象学明见性、柏拉图真理之暴力，到笛卡尔恶魔与街头闲谈中的「琐碎之真」，一场关于真理、想象力、权力与日常生活的深度对谈
summary_en: The one-year anniversary special of Iambus: two hosts improvise answers to a French philosophy baccalauréat question — 'Is truth always convincing?' From whether the Earth is round or flat, phenomenological evidence, and the violence of Platonic truth, to Descartes' evil demon and the 'trivial truths' of street-corner chat, this is a deep conversation about truth, imagination, power, and everyday life.

scenes.title_cn: 一、节目形式与核心命题
scenes.title_en: The Format and the Core Question
scenes.context: 介绍节目玩法：随机抽题、15分钟准备、即兴作答、禁止学术黑话。语域：casual 播客幕后 + 哲学入门。
scenes.speak: The producer Achai picks a question at random; the hosts get only about fifteen minutes to prepare, then answer it impromptu as a conversation — it's like a game. There's no scoring; whoever violates the rules too often — abusing jargon or name-dropping philosophers — has to buy books out of their own pocket. Academic words like '-ism,' '-ity,' and 'tradition' are deliberately banned, forcing them to discuss philosophy in everyday language and testing their dialogue and improvisation skills. This is modeled on the French baccalauréat philosophy essay — the prompt being 'La vérité est-elle toujours convaincante?' — is truth always convincing? As they said, they were answering a philosophy exam, but they couldn't answer in an overly academic, scholarly way. The French philosophy exam is famous for open-ended essays: define the concept, argue, then answer the counterarguments — but this show deliberately breaks that rigid template. And everyday experience shows why: some people are convinced the Earth is flat and argue about wrong arithmetic answers on Douyin — even the most 'obvious' truth can't convince everyone. Money is persuasive, lies are persuasive — but is a triangle persuasive? Is one plus one equals two persuasive?

sentences.cn: 核心机制：制作人阿柴随机抽题，主播仅有约15分钟准备，随后以对谈形式即兴作答——类似游戏，无法打分，违规多者（滥用专业词汇、超额提哲学家名字）需自掏腰包送书
sentences.en: Core mechanism: producer Achai draws a question at random; the hosts get about 15 minutes to prepare, then answer it impromptu as a dialogue — like a game. There's no scoring, and whoever breaks the rules too often (jargon abuse, name-dropping philosophers) pays for the books out of their own pocket.
sentences.note: 表达提示draw a question → 随机抽题；impromptu → 即兴；jargon abuse → 滥用专业词汇；name-drop → 炫耀性地提名人

sentences.cn: 关键理解：刻意禁止「主义」「性」「传统」等学术词汇，迫使用日常语言讨论哲学，检验对话与随机应变能力
sentences.en: Key insight: academic words like '-ism,' '-ity,' and 'tradition' are deliberately banned, forcing them to talk philosophy in everyday language and testing real dialogue and improvisation.
sentences.note: 表达提示deliberately banned → 刻意禁止；everyday language → 日常语言；improvisation → 随机应变

sentences.cn: 典型场景：法国高中毕业会考（Bac）哲学论述题，本题原文为 La vérité est-elle toujours convaincante?（真理是否总是具有说服力？）
sentences.en: Typical scenario: the French high-school leaving exam (Bac) philosophy essay — the original prompt here is 'La vérité est-elle toujours convaincante?' — is truth always convincing?
sentences.note: 表达提示leaving exam (Bac) → 高中毕业会考；essay prompt → 论述题；convincing → 有说服力

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「我们虽然是在答哲学高考题，但是我们不能以过分学院派的学术的方式去回答。」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'We are answering a philosophy exam question, but we can't answer it in an overly academic, scholarly way.'
sentences.note: 表达提示academic/scholarly → 学院派的；answer in a way → 以…方式作答

sentences.cn: （引用）相关概念：法国哲学高考以开放性论述著称，考生需先定义概念、再论证、最后回应反驳——但本节目刻意打破这一八股框架
sentences.en: Related concept: the French philosophy exam is famous for open-ended essays — define the concept, argue, then address the rebuttal — but this show deliberately breaks that rigid template.
sentences.note: 表达提示open-ended essay → 开放性论述；rebuttal → 反驳；rigid template → 八股框架

sentences.cn: 从日常经验出发——有人坚信地球是平的、在抖音上为错误算术答案争吵——可见再「显然」的真理也无法说服所有人。「金钱很有说服力，谎言很有说服力，但三角形很有说服力吗？1+1=2 有说服力吗？」
sentences.en: Start from daily life: some people are convinced the Earth is flat and argue over wrong arithmetic answers on Douyin — even the most 'obvious' truth can't convince everyone. 'Money is convincing, lies are convincing — but is a triangle convincing? Is 1+1=2 convincing?'
sentences.note: 表达提示flat-Earther → 地平说信奉者；the most obvious truth → 最显然的真理；persuasive/convincing → 有说服力

paraphrase.intent: 想说「限制越多，对话越真实」
phrases: The stricter the ban, the more honest the conversation.
Banned jargon forced them to actually think and talk.
paraphrase.chunks: stricter ban, more honest talk · forced to think and talk
paraphrase.usage: 第一句做结论，第二句讲原因

paraphrase.intent: 想说「再显然的真理也不能说服所有人」
phrases: Even the most obvious truth fails to convince everyone.
Some people will argue with you about 1+1=2.
paraphrase.chunks: obvious truth fails to convince · argue about 1+1=2
paraphrase.usage: 第一句是论点，第二句是具体例证

scenes.title_cn: 二、地球是圆的吗？三种理解路径
scenes.title_en: Is the Earth Round? Three Paths to Understanding
scenes.context: Andy 用剃刀原则、郁彤用想象力与权力，两个视角回答「为什么我们相信地球是圆的」。语域：casual 哲学对谈。
scenes.speak: Andy argues with Occam's razor — the 'razor principle,' as they call it. If the Earth were flat, you'd need to invent elaborate conspiracies; the simpler explanation is to accept a spherical Earth. But we never actually ran the shadow experiment ourselves — what we call 'verification' is really a hermeneutic inference made in a specific historical and social context. Scientific truths are established through peer review, yet ordinary people believe the Earth is round not because they've read the papers, but because they've been told so since childhood. Yutong, by contrast, stresses imagination and power. To her, truth is boring, theoretical, unrelated to her — she believes the Earth is round not from scientific verification but because language and childhood education have implanted a 'spherical Earth' in her imagination; imagining a flat Earth is extremely hard. As she said, the proposition 'the Earth is round' is convincing because it seizes me through imagination, not because truth itself seizes me. Andy pushes back: it's not so much truth that's persuasive as power — schools and the scientific establishment drill 'the Earth is a sphere' into you, and these institutions of knowledge transmission sustain the belief. In the Middle Ages, people believing in a flat Earth was likewise the work of particular institutions of power.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：Andy 用奥卡姆剃刀（节目中称「剃刀原则」）论证：若假设大地是平的，需增设阴谋团体等复杂实体；更简洁的解释是接受「大地是球体」。但我们并未亲手做过太阳夹角实验，所谓「验证」实为特定历史社会语境下的解释学推断
sentences.en: Core mechanism: Andy uses Occam's razor (they call it the 'razor principle'): if the Earth were flat, you'd need complex conspiracies; the simpler explanation is to accept a spherical Earth. But we never did the sun-angle experiment ourselves — what we call 'verification' is really a hermeneutic inference under a specific historical-social context.
sentences.note: 表达提示Occam's razor → 奥卡姆剃刀；conspiracy → 阴谋团体；hermeneutic inference → 解释学推断

sentences.cn: 关键理解：科学真理经同行评议确立，但普通人相信地球是圆，未必因为读过论文，而是因为从小被如此告知
sentences.en: Key insight: scientific truth is established through peer review, but ordinary people believe the Earth is round not because they've read the papers — they believe it because they've been told so since childhood.
sentences.note: 表达提示peer review → 同行评议；been told since childhood → 从小被告知

sentences.cn: （引用）与郁彤观点对比：Andy 侧重可验证性与逻辑简洁；郁彤侧重想象力与权力塑造
sentences.en: Comparison: Andy focuses on verifiability and logical simplicity; Yutong focuses on imagination and the shaping power of institutions.
sentences.note: 表达提示verifiability → 可验证性；logical simplicity → 逻辑简洁；shaping power → 塑造力

sentences.cn: 郁彤认为「真理是无聊的、理论的、与我没关系」——她相信地球是圆的，不是因为科学验证，而是因为语言与童年教育已将「球体地球」植入想象力；想象一个平的地球极其困难
sentences.en: Yutong thinks 'truth is boring, theoretical, and has nothing to do with me' — she believes the Earth is round not from scientific verification but because language and childhood education have planted a 'spherical Earth' in her imagination; imagining a flat Earth is extremely hard.
sentences.note: 表达提示planted in imagination → 植入想象力；childhood education → 童年教育；has nothing to do with me → 与我无关

sentences.cn: （引用）「所谓地球是圆的这个命题很有说服力，是因为它通过想象力抓住了我，而不是真理本身抓住了我。」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'The proposition that the Earth is round is convincing because it seizes me through imagination — not because truth itself seizes me.'
sentences.note: 表达提示seize me through imagination → 通过想象力抓住我

sentences.cn: Andy 追问：与其说真理有说服力，不如说权力有说服力——学校、科学体制反复教授「大地是球体」，知识传承机构维持着这一信念。中世纪众人信大地是平的，同样是特定权力机构的作用
sentences.en: Andy pushes back: it's less truth that is persuasive than power — schools and the scientific establishment drill 'the Earth is a sphere' into you, and institutions of knowledge transmission maintain the belief. In the Middle Ages, belief in a flat Earth was equally the work of particular institutions of power.
sentences.note: 表达提示push back → 反驳；scientific establishment → 科学体制；drill into → 反复灌输；institutions of power → 权力机构

paraphrase.intent: 想说「更简洁的解释更有力」
phrases: The simpler explanation tends to win.
Occam's razor keeps the story lean.
paraphrase.chunks: simpler explanation wins · Occam's razor keeps it lean
paraphrase.usage: 第一句直白，第二句点名术语

paraphrase.intent: 想说「让人相信的往往是权力而不是真理」
phrases: What convinces is often power, not truth.
Authority repeats, and repetition becomes belief.
paraphrase.chunks: power not truth · repetition becomes belief
paraphrase.usage: 第一句是核心论点，第二句展开机制

scenes.title_cn: 三、哲学史上寻求「有说服力之真理」的尝试
scenes.title_en: Attempts in the History of Philosophy to Find 'Persuasive Truth'
scenes.context: 现象学明见性、形式化科学、柏拉图洞穴——哲学史上三种寻求自明真理的路径。语域：casual 哲学史讲解。
scenes.speak: First, phenomenology: don't ask whether red is 'really' red — just confirm 'I clearly saw red.' What is seen is itself persuasive; that's the self-evident standard phenomenology tries to establish. This works for everyday perceptual judgments, but evidence can't cover the complex web of interests in real arguments. As they said, what did we actually see... when a thing is merely seen, it is quite persuasive. Second, formalizing science — like one plus one equals two — so everyone can verify truth under the same rules. Yutong points out that a circle, as a theoretical entity, can be given form through imagination, but concepts like wave-particle duality resist being imagined. Formal logic works for mathematics, but it can't capture the complexity and emotional dimension of real-world facts. And then there's Plato's cave: truth is the sun that you see — and seeing it 'blinds' you, you're completely conquered and silenced. This truth isn't a comfortable everyday perception like seeing a red coat; it's a forceful persuasion whose result is the total overturning of your existing beliefs.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：不追问「红色是否真红」，只确认「我明明看见了红色」——被看到之物本身即具说服力，是现象学试图建立的自明真理标准
sentences.en: Core mechanism: don't ask whether red is 'really' red — only confirm 'I clearly saw red.' What is seen is itself persuasive — that's the self-evident standard phenomenology tries to establish.
sentences.note: 表达提示phenomenology → 现象学；self-evident → 自明的；persuasive → 有说服力

sentences.cn: 典型场景：日常知觉判断；但明见性无法涵盖生活争论的复杂利益纠葛
sentences.en: Typical scenario: everyday perceptual judgments — but evidence cannot cover the complex tangle of interests in real-life disputes.
sentences.note: 表达提示perceptual judgment → 知觉判断；tangle of interests → 利益纠葛；cover → 涵盖

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「我们到底看到了什么……当这个东西只是被看到的时候，他就是很有说服力的。」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'What did we actually see... when something is merely seen, it is quite persuasive.'
sentences.note: 表达提示merely seen → 只是被看到；persuasive → 有说服力

sentences.cn: 核心机制：将科学高度形式化（如 1+1=2），使所有人可按同一规则检验真伪。郁彤指出圆作为理论实体可通过想象赋予形式，但波粒二象性等概念难以被想象把握
sentences.en: Core mechanism: formalize science (like 1+1=2) so everyone can verify truth by the same rules. Yutong notes a circle, as a theoretical entity, can be given form by imagination, but concepts like wave-particle duality are hard to grasp imaginatively.
sentences.note: 表达提示formalize → 形式化；theoretical entity → 理论实体；wave-particle duality → 波粒二象性

sentences.cn: 适用边界：形式逻辑对数学有效，但不足以展现现实生活中事实的复杂性与情感维度
sentences.en: Boundary: formal logic works for mathematics but is insufficient for the complexity and emotional dimension of facts in real life.
sentences.note: 表达提示formal logic → 形式逻辑；emotional dimension → 情感维度；insufficient → 不足以

sentences.cn: 柏拉图洞穴寓言中，真理是被看到的太阳——看见时你会「瞎了」，被彻底征服、压口无言。这种真理不是舒适的日常知觉（如看到红衣服），而是以完全改变既有信念为结果的强力说服
sentences.en: In Plato's cave allegory, truth is the sun you see — seeing it 'blinds' you, you are wholly conquered and silenced. This truth isn't a comfortable everyday perception (like seeing a red coat) but a forceful persuasion whose outcome is the complete overturning of your prior beliefs.
sentences.note: 表达提示cave allegory → 洞穴寓言；conquered and silenced → 被征服、哑口无言；overturn beliefs → 颠覆信念

paraphrase.intent: 想说「眼见为实是现象学的自明标准」
phrases: What you see is persuasive simply by being seen.
Evidence doesn't ask permission — it's just there.
paraphrase.chunks: seen = persuasive · evidence needs no permission
paraphrase.usage: 第一句贴合原文，第二句更俏皮

paraphrase.intent: 想说「柏拉图式的真理会把人灼伤」
phrases: Platonic truth hits you like staring into the sun.
Some truths conquer rather than comfort.
paraphrase.chunks: like staring into the sun · conquer rather than comfort
paraphrase.usage: 第一句比喻形象，第二句做对比总结

scenes.title_cn: 四、笛卡尔：本体论证明与恶灵
scenes.title_en: Descartes: The Ontological Argument and the Evil Demon
scenes.context: 笛卡尔的本体论证明为何今天无人接受，以及「被真理穿透」的感觉如何依赖历史语境。语域：casual 哲学史对谈。
scenes.speak: The ontological argument infers from the idea of perfection that a perfect being — God — must exist. Descartes, a top-tier mathematician, insisted this proof was as indubitable as 'the angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees' — yet almost nobody accepts it today. The feeling of 'being pierced by truth' is deeply dependent on historical context and cannot serve as an absolute standard. As Yutong reads it, what's truly powerful about Descartes is the 'evil demon' image — a crimson, bat-winged demon that jams everyone's vision; believing in God may stem from an existential predicament rather than logical necessity. But there's a caution: reducing a believer's sincere pursuit to natural causes like fear and desire can disrespect the other person — Descartes would 'angrily' deny that his belief in the ontological argument wasn't genuine. The resolution: admit both sides may be equally caught in the age's 'demon' — the Zeitgeist — and neither is superior. The tension between hermeneutic reduction and respect for sincerity always remains.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：从「完满观念」推断必存在完满存在者（上帝）。笛卡尔作为顶尖数学家，却坚称此证明如「三角形内角和180度」般不可怀疑——但今天几乎无人接受
sentences.en: Core mechanism: from the 'idea of perfection' infer that a perfect being — God — must exist. Descartes, a brilliant mathematician, insisted this proof was as indubitable as 'angles of a triangle summing to 180 degrees' — yet almost nobody accepts it today.
sentences.note: 表达提示ontological argument → 本体论证明；idea of perfection → 完满观念；indubitable → 不可怀疑

sentences.cn: 关键理解：「被真理穿透的感觉」高度依赖历史语境，不可作为绝对标准
sentences.en: Key insight: the feeling of 'being pierced by truth' is heavily dependent on historical context and cannot serve as an absolute standard.
sentences.note: 表达提示pierced by truth → 被真理穿透；historical context → 历史语境；absolute standard → 绝对标准

sentences.cn: （引用）与郁彤解读：笛卡尔真正有力的是「恶灵」想象——通体红色、蝙蝠翅膀的恶魔扰乱所有人视线；相信上帝或许源于生存论困境而非逻辑必然
sentences.en: Yutong's reading: what is genuinely powerful in Descartes is the 'evil demon' imagination — a crimson, bat-winged demon that confounds everyone's vision. Believing in God may spring from an existential predicament rather than logical necessity.
sentences.note: 表达提示evil demon → 恶灵；existential predicament → 生存论困境；logical necessity → 逻辑必然

sentences.cn: 原因：将信徒的真诚追求还原为恐惧、欲望等自然原因，可能不尊重对方——笛卡尔会「生气地」否认自己并非真心相信本体论证明
sentences.en: Why it can offend: reducing a believer's sincere pursuit to natural causes such as fear and desire may fail to respect them — Descartes would 'angrily' deny he didn't genuinely believe the ontological argument.
sentences.note: 表达提示reduce to → 还原为；sincere pursuit → 真诚的追求；fail to respect → 不尊重

sentences.cn: 解法：承认双方可能同样陷入时代「恶魔」（Zeitgeist）的掌控，没有谁更高明
sentences.en: The resolution: admit both sides may be equally under the spell of the age's 'demon' (the Zeitgeist) — neither is smarter than the other.
sentences.note: 表达提示under the spell of → 受…掌控；Zeitgeist → 时代精神；neither is superior → 没有谁更高明

sentences.cn: 严重程度：小心——解释学还原与尊重真诚之间的张力始终存在
sentences.en: Severity: be careful — the tension between hermeneutic reduction and respect for sincerity is always there.
sentences.note: 表达提示hermeneutic reduction → 解释学还原；tension → 张力；sincerity → 真诚

paraphrase.intent: 想说「笛卡尔认为自己的证明像数学一样不容置疑」
phrases: He treated his proof as self-evident as a math theorem.
To him, God's existence was as obvious as 180 degrees.
paraphrase.chunks: as self-evident as a theorem · as obvious as 180 degrees
paraphrase.usage: 第一句客观，第二句更形象

paraphrase.intent: 想说「被真理穿透的感觉有时空局限性」
phrases: The sense of being pierced by truth varies across eras.
What feels self-evident in one age looks odd in another.
paraphrase.chunks: varies across eras · self-evident in one age, odd in another
paraphrase.usage: 第一句是结论，第二句展开举例

scenes.title_cn: 五、日常之真：琐碎真相的力量
scenes.title_en: Everyday Truth: The Power of Trivial Truths
scenes.context: 从拉丁语词源「三岔路口」到打招呼的权力结构，日常琐碎之真如何保存无法被抹去的真实。语域：casual 文化观察 + 语言学趣谈。
scenes.speak: Trivia comes from the Latin for 'three-way crossroads' — the 'this and that' people exchange when they run into each other at the corner. Archives can be rewritten, but a passing remark or a nod in an encounter on the street often preserves a reality that can't be erased. As they said, in everyday conversations between people, a great deal of truth is preserved. Althusser argued that 'hailing' — interpellation — carries an element of subjection: calling someone Mr. or Mrs. already slots them into a gender order. Judith Butler tells of being routinely misaddressed as male; people are confused when they can't classify you. But a nod or a smile may involve no categorization at all — just recognition. A plain 'nihao' can be deeply offensive to some overseas Chinese — it unilaterally labels you 'Chinese,' a power move of subjective definition. And take the Guangzhou tornado: a friend described 'fire floating in the sky.' Literally absurd — yet the listener instantly knows there's no reason to lie at that moment. The absurdity itself hints that some real experience must lie behind it, even if the words aren't literally true. Stories passed mouth to mouth, oddities in anonymous notes — they aren't fiction because they grew through natural circulation; their absurd surface may be buried history trying to declare its truth.

sentences.cn: 核心机制：Trivia 源自拉丁语「三岔路口」——人们在路口偶遇交谈的「有的没的」之事。历史档案可被篡改，但街头偶遇时的一句闲话、一个点头，往往保存着无法被抹去的真实
sentences.en: Core mechanism: trivia comes from the Latin for 'three-way crossroads' — the 'this and that' of chance conversations at the street corner. Archives can be tampered with, but a passing remark or a nod in a chance encounter often preserves a reality that cannot be erased.
sentences.note: 表达提示trivia → 琐碎之事（词源：三岔路口）；three-way crossroads → 三岔路口；passing remark → 一句闲话；tamper with → 篡改

sentences.cn: （引用）原文依据：「在人与人之间的日常交谈当中……有很多真的东西被保存了下来。」
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'In everyday conversation between people... a great deal of truth gets preserved.'
sentences.note: 表达提示everyday conversation → 日常交谈；preserve truth → 保存真实

sentences.cn: 阿尔都塞称「打招呼」（interpellation）内含使人臣服之意——称呼 Mr./Mrs. 已将对方置入性别秩序。Judith Butler 讲述常被误称男性的经历：无法完成定性时人们感到困惑。但点头、微笑可能不涉及归类，只是表达承认
sentences.en: Althusser held that 'hailing' (interpellation) implies subjection — calling someone Mr. or Mrs. already places them in a gender order. Judith Butler describes being routinely misaddressed as male: people are confused when they can't classify you. Yet a nod or a smile may involve no classification at all — only recognition.
sentences.note: 表达提示interpellation → 招呼/询唤；subjection → 臣服；gender order → 性别秩序；misaddress → 称呼错

sentences.cn: （引用）「你好」对海外华人有时极具冒犯性——单方面将你界定为「中国人」，是一种主观定义的权力行为
sentences.en: Direct quote: 'Nihao' can be deeply offensive to some overseas Chinese — it unilaterally defines you as 'Chinese,' an act of power through subjective labeling.
sentences.note: 表达提示unilaterally → 单方面；subjective labeling → 主观定义；offensive → 冒犯性

sentences.cn: 核心机制：广州龙卷风时，朋友描述「火在天上飘」——字面不可思议，但听者立刻意识到对方没必要在此刻撒谎；荒诞本身暗示背后必有某种真实经验，哪怕字面不真
sentences.en: Core mechanism: during the Guangzhou tornado, a friend described 'fire floating in the sky' — literally absurd, but the listener instantly knows there's no reason to lie at that moment. The absurdity itself signals that some real experience must lie behind it, even if the words aren't literally true.
sentences.note: 表达提示literally absurd → 字面不可思议；lie behind → 背后必有；no reason to lie → 没必要撒谎

sentences.cn: 典型场景：口耳相传的故事、无名笔记中的奇闻——故事非虚构，因其在自然流传中生长，荒诞面相可能是被掩埋的历史在试图宣告真相
sentences.en: Typical scenario: stories passed mouth to mouth, oddities in anonymous notes — they're not fiction because they grew through natural circulation; their absurd surface may be buried history trying to announce its truth.
sentences.note: 表达提示mouth to mouth → 口耳相传；natural circulation → 自然流传；buried history → 被掩埋的历史

paraphrase.intent: 想说「街头偶遇的闲话保存着真实」
phrases: A chance remark on the street can outlast any archive.
Real truth often lives in passing talk, not official records.
paraphrase.chunks: chance remark outlasts archives · truth lives in passing talk
paraphrase.usage: 第一句有力度，第二句直白总结

paraphrase.intent: 想说「打招呼也是一种权力动作」
phrases: Even a greeting can be a power move.
Labeling someone 'Chinese' is an act of definition.
paraphrase.chunks: greeting as power move · labeling is an act of definition
paraphrase.usage: 第一句概括，第二句落回具体例子

practice.cn: 用「draw a question」说：制作人随机抽题。
practice.en: The producer draws a philosophy question at random.

practice.cn: 用「self-evident」说：被看到之物本身就是自明的。
practice.en: What is merely seen is self-evidently persuasive.

practice.cn: 用「push back」说：Andy 反驳说真正有说服力的是权力。
practice.en: Andy pushes back, arguing that what convinces is power, not truth.

practice.cn: 用「interpellation」说：打招呼内含使人臣服之意。
practice.en: Interpellation — even a simple greeting — carries an element of subjection.

pitfalls.wrong: The truth is very persuasive, so everyone believes it.
pitfalls.right: Even the most self-evident truth fails to convince everyone.
pitfalls.why: 第一期核心论点恰恰是「真理不一定有说服力」；直译会让结论与原意相反。

pitfalls.wrong: Descartes thought God's existence is very obvious.
pitfalls.right: Descartes insisted the proof was as indubitable as a mathematical theorem.
pitfalls.why: obvious 太弱；「不可怀疑」用 indubitable / beyond doubt 才贴合哲学论证语境。

pitfalls.wrong: The truth catches me through imagination.
pitfalls.right: The proposition seizes me through imagination, not because truth itself seizes me.
pitfalls.why: catch 是「抓住」，此处是「征服/俘获」，用 seize/grip；且要保留「不是真理本身抓住我」的对比。

pitfalls.wrong: A greeting means you are a power behavior.
pitfalls.right: Even a greeting can be an act of power — a unilateral act of definition.
pitfalls.why: 「是一种权力动作」用 act of power / power move，不是 is a power behavior。

shifts.before: 以为科学真理=经过验证的事实，大家自然就信
shifts.after: 多数人信「地球是圆的」不是因为读过论文，而是因为从小被权力机构灌输

shifts.before: 以为哲学证明只要能自洽就永远有效
shifts.after: 「被真理穿透的感觉」高度依赖历史语境——笛卡尔的证明今天已无人接受

shifts.before: 以为「你好」「点头」只是无害的礼貌
shifts.after: 打招呼内含命名与分类的权力——主观定义本身就是一种冒犯可能
